messages:
eli: Escalation from customer Noteable — long streaming responses get cut mid-stream when user switches WiFi -> cellular on iOS. Customer sees partial JSON, no client reconnect. Ticket #12345. Repro steps below.

eli: Repro steps they sent:
1) Open iOS app on WiFi, start a long generation (30s+).
2) Toggle airplane mode on/off or switch to cellular during the stream.
3) Client displays "stream closed by server" and only partial output returned.

eli: Minimal curl reproduction they tried:
```
curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \n  -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \n  "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream?model=gptx-long"
```
They send continuously and see initial chunks then abrupt end.

maria: Thanks, can you paste the request-id and server-side request log for one incident? Need timestamps to correlate with our proxies.

eli: Request-id: rq_7f9d3a. Server log shows upstream: "client disconnected (ECONNRESET)" and envoy: "upstream prematurely closed connection" at 2024-11-02T18:23:45Z. Customer attached pcap: https://s3.redwood/support/pcaps/12345.pcap

jin: Looking at logs — on our side token TTL was valid, no auth 401. This looks like a client-side TCP close during NAT handoff. iOS sometimes tears sockets when switching networks. Do they run our hosted SDK? Which version?

eli: They use RN app with redwood-js 0.14. They said SDK doesn't auto-reconnect currently for SSE.

sam: Envoy/edge config notes: our streaming idle_timeout = 60s, proxy_send_timeout = 90s. Envoy TCP keepalive configurable but some mobile carriers drop NAT after ~30s if no bytes. We normally send SSE comments every 20s for hosted customers to keep NAT alive. Are keepalives enabled for this account?

jin: Good catch — for this Dedicated cluster, keepalive comments were disabled due to a previous bug in the ingress rollout. So on network handoff the carrier sees an idle connection and resets. Two remediation tracks: server-side keepalive (quick) and client-side reconnect (medium).

eli: Customer asked for immediate workaround they can ship: any low-friction options?

jin: Recommended immediate steps to customer:
- Upgrade SDK to 0.15 which includes simple reconnect + resume token support.
- Server: re-enable SSE keepalive comments for their Dedicated pool (we can flip per-account).
- As a stopgap, increase token TTL to 120s to avoid auth races during reconnects.

maria: Also suggest app-level: implement idempotency for partial-chunk resume (stitching by server-provided chunk ids) and exponential reconnect with random jitter.

eli: I posted the steps to the customer. They asked if we can enable keepalives on their dedicated cluster now.

sam: I'm patching the ingress: starting canary to enable keepalive-comments for acct "noteable" (canary 10%). Patch id: enable-ssr-keepalive-2325.

deploy-bot: rollout started: enable-ssr-keepalive-2325 -> targeting /dedicated/pool/noteable : canary=10% (2024-11-02T19:05:00Z)

jin: After enabling keepalives we should see fewer abrupt resets. Also add an observability metric: `sse_keepalive_sent` per pool and `stream_resume_attempts` to track client reconnects. I'll add an eval alert for >5% mid-stream disconnect rate.

eli: Customer confirmed after patch: better but still occasional disconnects during very fast handoffs. They've prioritized SDK upgrade and will roll 0.15 next week.

maria: Ok — action items: 
- sam: finish keepalive canary and promote to 100% for noteable (DRI: sam)
- jin: add metrics & alert for stream disconnects (DRI: jin)
- eli: follow up with customer and collect a couple more PCAPs if problems persist (DRI: eli)

maria: :thumbsup:

eli: Marking this as resolved for now pending SDK rollout and metrics. Will reopen if customer repros after upgrade.
